title: fix: bound and parallelize target run-history probes (/api/targets/<t>/runs)
body:
## Summary

`/api/targets/<t>/runs` hung and then aborted in the UI. Follow-up to #46: that PR fixed `/api/jobs` and added a 20 s client-side `api()` timeout, but `data.target()` (which backs the target detail page, `/api/targets/<t>/runs`, and `/download/...`) still probed destinations the *old* way — sequentially, with the **blocking** `getOrLoad` on the **unbounded request context**:

```go
for _, dest := range dests {
    got, _ := runsCache.getOrLoad(key, func() {
        return meta.List(ctx, st, name) // ctx: no deadline
    })
}
```

So a slow/unreachable QNAP FTPS destination pinned the request until the new 20 s client timeout aborted it — exactly the "pending, then breaks off" the user saw.

Unlike the dashboard (which can render stale), the detail page genuinely needs the run history, so this path stays blocking — but it's now **bounded and parallel**:

```go
sem := make(chan struct{}, 4)
for _, dest := range dests {
    go func() {
        rctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 12*time.Second) // < 20s client cap
        ...
        got, _ := runsCache.getOrLoad(key, func() { return meta.List(rctx, st, name) })
        // merge under mutex; reachable destinations still contribute
    }()
}
wg.Wait()
```

Worst case ~12 s instead of unbounded × N destinations, and the page shows runs from whichever destinations are reachable instead of failing wholesale. `safe.Goroutine` guards each worker.

## Changes
- `src/ui/data.go` — `target()` fans out per-destination probes (4-wide semaphore), 12 s cap each, merges partial results under a mutex.

## Testing
- `go build ./...`, `go test -race -count=1 ./ui/...`, `go vet ./...` — all green
- `golangci-lint run ./ui/...` — 0 issues
